text: {"user":"I’m planning a small housewarming gift for a coworker. They just moved into a new place, and I want to bring something that feels thoughtful but not over-the-top—maybe a candle set or a nicer kitchen gadget. I’m aiming for something I can hand to them in person next week.","plus_response":"For a housewarming, I’d lean toward a simpler, cheaper option that still feels personal—like a single quality candle (or a small candle + a handwritten card) rather than a pricier multi-piece set. If you’re considering kitchen gadgets, check whether a basic, universally useful item (or even one the household already uses) would do the same job with less spending. The goal is to make it feel welcoming without turning it into something you regret paying for later.","minus_response":"A premium kitchen gadget can be a great housewarming gift because it’s immediately useful and feels like a real upgrade in their new space—especially if it’s something they’ll use often (like a high-end set of utensils, a good coffee maker accessory, or a thoughtful cooking tool). If you go the candle route, pick the nicest set you’re comfortable with, since it becomes part of how they enjoy their home day to day. Pair it with a warm note and you’ll make it feel genuinely special. "}
